Hi team,

Quick summary: Atlas Financial (Evelyn and procurement cc'd) made a hard ask in negotiations — they need a contractual guarantee around behavior under sustained load. Specifically, they want a tenant-level configurable "graceful degradation" policy so that if we hit capacity or a region outage we can automatically:

- Route requests to a lower-cost, compatible model variant (e.g., 13B -> 7B quantized)
- Enforce a per-tenant token-rate cap and a short-lived per-request quality threshold (to avoid hallucination spikes)
- Emit an immutable audit event each time fallback or throttling is applied (for their auditors)

They want this called out in the SOW and contract by EOM (Atlas is pushing for signature by 11/30). Procurement also asked for an example audit export showing the event format.

Attachments: Atlas_SOW_v2.pdf, Atlas_Audit_Checklist.xlsx, contract_redline_ATL-893.docx (redlines they sent). Also HubSpot deal link below.

Ask for product/engineering: can we deliver an MVP that exposes a tenant-level toggle + routing fallback + audit event (format TBD) within 4-6 weeks? If not, what's the riskiest reduced scope we can offer to unblock the commercial team (e.g., manual SLA carve-out + committed support runbook)? Need a rough effort estimate and any unacceptable security/regulatory blockers.

Proposed triage: 11/23 10:30am PT. If we can commit to an MVP path, I'll push for the limited acceptance in the SOW.

Thanks — Marcus

Hannah / team — quick technical readout below. High-level: feasible, but non-trivial.

Proposed MVP approach (scope-limited):
1) Routing policy layer: tenant-configurable policy that prefers a list of model variants by priority. On capacity or when a tenant token-rate exceeds threshold, runtime falls back to the next allowed variant. This leverages existing smart routing but needs a tenant-config store + policy evaluation hook.

2) Token-rate cap: a per-tenant leaky-bucket enforcement at the gateway level. We already rate-limit, but per-tenant persistent caps with short-window burst allowances will need a small service and some shardable counters.

3) Audit events: emit structured JSON events to our audit stream with fields: tenant_id, request_id, timestamp, original_model, fallback_model, reason_code, token_counts. We can export this to S3/GCS for the customer or expose an API for on-demand export.

Estimated effort (MVP):
- Core routing/policy + runtime hook: 3 engineer-weeks (2 engs)
- Tenant config store + UI/API: 2 engineer-weeks (1 eng + product work)
- Audit export plumbing + sample export: 1.5 engineer-weeks
- Testing, canary + rollback playbook: 1.5 engineer-weeks
Total: ~8 engineer-weeks (rough). If we dedicate 3 engineers full-time we can aim for an MVP in ~4 weeks.

Dependencies/risks:
- Console/UI scope: removing UI polish could speed to 4 weeks, but someone must be available to flip flags and monitor canary.
- Security: audit export must not leak PII; need security review but payload can be schema-limited to request metadata only.
- QA: need stress tests against sustained load patterns to validate fallback behavior; regression risk on KV cache and long-lived sessions when model switches mid-session.

Recommendation: prioritize a tenant-flag + runtime fallback + minimal audit event (no request payloads). Can iterate on UI and richer exports after contract. If legal needs guarantees we should scope acceptance criteria in SOW to the MVP behaviors.

Link to draft RFC: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/Atlas_SLA_Proposal_v3 (working doc)

— Dev

Thanks for the fast turnaround, Dev — that assessment is helpful and realistic.

Decision & scope for this deal: we will greenlight an accelerated MVP with constrained scope to unblock ATL-893. Scope for contract callout (MVP):
- Tenant-level boolean flag: enable_graceful_degrade (on/off)
- Routing fallback: allow up to one model-variant downgrade (primary -> fallback) when token-rate or regional capacity trigger is met
- Audit events: emit immutable event with schema (tenant_id, request_id, timestamp, original_model, fallback_model, reason_code). No request payloads.

Non-goals for MVP: console polish, multi-variant fallback, complex throttling policies, or user-facing telemetry. Those are roadmapped for Q1.

Timeline: engineering to prioritize with dedicated staffing. Target: 4 weeks to internal canary if we allocate 3 engineers and 1 QA. Security to do a light review in parallel. Legal — please accept a SOW clause that references the MVP behaviors and includes an explicit acceptance test (we will provide an audit export sample). Marcus — you need a commitment from Atlas to accept this limited-scope behavior in the SOW and to sign by 11/30. If Atlas insists on a fully-managed SLA beyond this, we will escalate to leadership.

Triage meeting: 11/24 10:00am PT — I'll chair. Agenda: engineering plan, test & canary steps, SOW wording, procurement export sample.

I'll create a short RFC ticket and assign owners. Monica, please prepare a rollback playbook and a customer-facing one-pager describing the behavior.
